title: Ohio Paycheck Calculator 2026 – Salary After Tax
description: Estimate your Ohio take-home pay after federal income tax, Ohio state tax, municipal income taxes, school district taxes and payroll deductions.
heading: Ohio Paycheck Calculator

parts.markdown:
Our free **Ohio paycheck calculator** helps you estimate your take-home pay after federal taxes, Ohio income tax, applicable municipal income taxes and school district taxes. Enter your salary or hourly earnings to understand how much of your gross income you could receive on payday.

Ohio's local income tax system makes paycheck calculations particularly important. Two employees earning the same salary may receive different net pay because they live or work in different municipalities or school districts.

Whether you work in Columbus, Cleveland, Cincinnati, Dayton or a smaller Ohio community, this calculator can help you understand the deductions affecting your earnings.

## How to Use the Ohio Paycheck Calculator

Enter your annual salary if you receive fixed compensation. Hourly employees should enter their hourly rate and the number of regular and qualifying overtime hours worked.

Choose your pay frequency. Enter federal and Ohio income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

If you are subject to municipal or school district income taxes, enter the total amount withheld for the pay period.

Add retirement contributions, insurance premiums and other employee deductions where applicable.

Review the estimated results to see how much of your gross earnings remains after taxes and deductions.

For accurate local tax estimates, confirm your residence and work location rather than relying exclusively on your postal address.

## Ohio Payroll Taxes in 2026

Ohio employees may encounter several layers of payroll taxation.

Additional Medicare withholding may apply to higher-income employees.

Unlike states with only federal and state income taxes, Ohio requires particular attention to local taxation. An estimate that ignores municipal or school district taxes may overstate your actual take-home pay.

## How Ohio State Income Tax Works

Ohio reduced its highest individual income tax rate to 2.75% for the 2026 tax year.

The state's annual nonbusiness income tax calculation uses the following structure:

These thresholds apply to Ohio taxable nonbusiness income, not necessarily your total gross salary.

For example, an employee with $60,000 in Ohio taxable nonbusiness income would have an illustrative tax calculation of:

$332 + (($60,000 − $26,050) × 0.0275) = $1,265.63

This represents the annual tax schedule calculation before other applicable adjustments or credits. It is not automatically the amount an employer should withhold throughout the year.

Employers use Ohio's dedicated payroll withholding tables. The [Ohio Department of Taxation employer withholding page](https://tax.ohio.gov/business/employer-withholding) provides the schedules and effective dates.

The 2026 withholding tables changed on August 1, so the date of your paycheck matters when estimating historical payroll deductions.

## Understanding Ohio Municipal Income Tax

Many Ohio cities and villages impose municipal income taxes on qualifying employee earnings.

The tax rate and applicable withholding requirements depend on the municipality and the employee's circumstances.

For instance, an employee may live in one city but commute to another municipality for work. The work municipality may impose income tax, while the employee's residence municipality may have separate tax requirements.

Some municipalities offer credits for income tax paid elsewhere. However, the amount and availability of these credits vary.

Do not assume that working in one municipality eliminates your potential tax obligation in another.

### Municipal paycheck example

Suppose an employee has $2,000 of municipal taxable earnings during a pay period, and an applicable local tax rate of 2%.

The municipal tax would be:

$2,000 × 0.02 = $40

This is an illustrative calculation using a hypothetical tax rate.

Use [The Finder](https://tax.ohio.gov/finder) to identify applicable tax jurisdictions and rates. You can also consult the [Regional Income Tax Agency](https://www.ritaohio.com/) if your municipality participates in RITA.

## Ohio School District Income Tax

Ohio's school district income tax is another feature that can affect residents' take-home income.

Not every school district imposes this tax. Liability generally depends on whether you reside in a district that has enacted an income tax.

Ohio distinguishes between school districts using a traditional tax base and those using an earned income tax base.

Traditional-base districts generally apply withholding using the appropriate state wage base and exemptions. Earned-income-base districts use a flat withholding rate without reductions for personal exemptions.

These distinctions matter because two school districts with the same published tax rate may not produce identical withholding amounts.

Check your school district using Ohio's official tax jurisdiction lookup before entering the applicable details.

If you move during the year, review whether your school district tax obligations have changed.

## Federal Payroll Taxes for Ohio Employees

Ohio employees generally pay federal income tax, Social Security and Medicare in addition to applicable state and local taxes.

Federal income tax withholding depends on earnings, filing status, payroll frequency and Form W-4 adjustments.

Social Security applies to covered employee earnings at 6.2%, up to the 2026 annual wage limit of $184,500.

Regular Medicare withholding is 1.45% of covered earnings, without a standard annual wage ceiling.

Employers also generally withhold an additional 0.9% when covered Medicare wages exceed $200,000 from that employer during the calendar year.

Read the [IRS Employer's Tax Guide](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) for further information about federal payroll contributions.

## Ohio Paycheck Example: $65,000 Salary

An employee earning $65,000 annually would generally receive the following gross earnings:

Assuming a $2,500 biweekly paycheck is fully subject to ordinary Social Security and Medicare contributions:

Social Security: $155.00

Medicare: $36.25

Total federal payroll contributions: $191.25

Now suppose the employee is also subject to an illustrative municipal income tax of 2%, calculated on the full $2,500.

Municipal tax: $50.00

The remaining income would be $2,258.75 before federal income tax, Ohio income tax, applicable school district taxes and other deductions.

Your actual paycheck may be substantially different depending on your specific tax jurisdictions and withholding information.

## Ohio Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Ohio hourly employees can estimate earnings by multiplying their hourly rate by regular working hours and adding qualifying overtime compensation.

For example, an employee earning $22 per hour who works 40 regular hours and six overtime hours at time-and-a-half would earn:

Regular pay: $22 × 40 = $880

Overtime pay: $22 × 1.5 × 6 = $198

Total gross pay: $1,078

Taxes and deductions are then calculated from the appropriate taxable wage amounts.

Not every worker qualifies for overtime compensation. Review the [US Department of Labor overtime guidance](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) if you are uncertain about your employment classification.

## Working Across Ohio State Borders

Ohio shares borders with several states, making interstate commuting relatively common.

Employees working across state lines may be affected by reciprocal income tax agreements, nonresident withholding rules and local tax obligations.

A reciprocal agreement can change which state generally receives income tax withholding on employee compensation.

However, it does not automatically remove every local tax obligation.

If you live outside Ohio but work for an Ohio employer, or live in Ohio while working elsewhere, confirm the applicable rules and withholding certificates with your payroll department.

The calculator should not be treated as a complete multi-state tax return estimator.

## Other Deductions From Ohio Paychecks

Your paycheck may include employee retirement contributions, health insurance premiums, dental coverage, flexible spending account contributions and other deductions.

Some deductions reduce taxable wages, while others are deducted after taxes have been calculated.

For example, a qualifying traditional retirement contribution may lower income-taxable earnings without reducing ordinary Social Security withholding.

Local taxable wage definitions may also differ from federal income tax definitions.

Review your actual pay stub when entering deductions into an Ohio salary calculator.

## Planning Your Budget Around Ohio Take-Home Pay

Your net paycheck is generally a more useful budgeting figure than your gross annual salary.

Before accepting a new job, estimate the impact of local taxes, commuting costs and employee benefits. A position offering higher gross pay may not provide a proportionately higher disposable income.

If you receive biweekly paychecks, remember that most months contain two payments, while some contain three.

Build a budget using your ordinary monthly cash flow, and consider allocating additional paychecks toward emergency savings or debt reduction.

Our [debt-to-income ratio calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) can help you evaluate borrowing commitments, while our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) can help establish a savings target.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the Ohio income tax rate in 2026?

Ohio's highest individual income tax rate for 2026 is 2.75%. The annual tax calculation includes a taxable-income threshold and a base tax amount. Payroll withholding follows separate official tables.

### Do all Ohio employees pay city income tax?

No. Municipal income tax depends on where you work, where you live and the applicable local rules. Some municipalities do not impose an income tax.

### How do I know whether I owe Ohio school district income tax?

Use Ohio's official tax jurisdiction lookup to identify your school district and confirm whether it imposes an income tax. Your school district and mailing address may not be identical.

## Estimate Your Ohio Take-Home Pay

Use our Ohio paycheck calculator to understand federal, state and applicable local payroll deductions before planning your spending or comparing employment opportunities.

The calculator provides estimates for educational purposes. Confirm complicated local or interstate tax obligations with the relevant tax authority or a qualified professional.
